paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Hounslow, including the council's own service, Foster Hounslow, and independent agencies. In November 2025 the council launched a recruitment campaign called "Grow in new ways", aimed at professionals, couples and single people over 30 who may never have thought about fostering, because the number of foster carers across the UK is falling.

The council's own criteria are clear. You need to be over 21, in good health, and live or work within reasonable reach of the borough, able to manage school runs, family time and health appointments. A spare room is needed if you want to foster children over two. You can rent, own or live in council housing (a private landlord has to agree in writing), and you can be single, married, LGBT+ or disabled. No qualifications are needed, since the council provides the training. Most people can keep working, but someone has to be at home full-time to foster a baby under two; respite care suits less flexible jobs.

Hounslow also looks after unaccompanied children seeking asylum, many of them from Afghanistan and Albania, and asks for carers willing to learn about a child's culture and support them through specialist training.

The council describes nine stages from first contact to approval, including Skills to Foster training, checks and six references, six to eight home visits from a social worker, and a fostering panel; it says the whole process usually takes four to six months. After approval you have a supervising social worker, support around the clock and continuing training, and a start-up grant is available for essential furniture. Talk to the council and two or three of the services above before choosing, and see the Ealing and London pages if you live near the borough's edge.

sources.title: Hounslow Council launches new fostering campaign to inspire a new generation of carers (Hounslow Council, 3 November 2025)
